'''Bruno [[Abdank coat of arms|Abdank]]-Abakanowicz''' (6 October 1852 – 29 August 1900) was a Polish [[mathematician]], [[inventor]], and [[electrical engineer]]. He is best known for inventing the [[integraph]] and contributing to the development of mathematical instruments and early electrification systems in France.

== Life ==
Abakanowicz was born in 1852 in [[Ukmergė]], then part of the [[Vilna Governorate]] of the [[Russian Empire]] (now [[Lithuania]]).<ref name="Bielerzewski">{{cite web | author=Piotr Bielerzewski | title=Wiłkomierz | publisher=own | year=2005 | work=Rzeczpospolita Wirtualna | url=http://rzecz-pospolita.com/wilkomierz0.php3 | access-date=2006-09-20 | language=pl | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070106204755/http://rzecz-pospolita.com/wilkomierz0.php3 | archive-date=2007-01-06 | url-status=dead }}</ref> 

After graduating from the [[Riga Technical University]], he completed his [[habilitation]]<ref name="Klaputh">{{cite journal | author=Ewa Klaputh | year=2006 | title=Le Château de Costaérès, czyli tajemnice inżyniera Abakanowicza | journal=Po Prostu | issue=22 | url=http://www.po-prostu.eu/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=310&Itemid=49 | access-date=2010-01-20 | language=pl | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110720171138/http://www.po-prostu.eu/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=310&Itemid=49 | archive-date=2011-07-20 }}</ref> and began working as an assistant at the [[Lviv Polytechnic|Technical University of Lwów]]. In 1881, he moved to [[France]],<ref name="Klaputh"/> where he purchased a villa in [[Saint-Maur-des-Fossés|Parc Saint-Maur]] on the outskirts of [[Paris]].

Earlier, Abakanowicz invented the [[integraph]], a mechanical device for drawing the integral of a curve, which was patented in 1880.<ref name="Abakanowicz">{{cite book | author=Bruno Abdank-Abakanowicz | title=Les intégraphes | year=1886 | publisher=Gauthier-Villars | location=Paris | url=https://archive.org/details/lesintgraphesla00abakgoog | language=fr }}</ref> It was later produced commercially by the Swiss firm ''Coradi''.<ref name="Bell">{{cite web | url=http://research.microsoft.com/~GBell/CyberMuseum_files%5CBell_Book_Files%5Cbooks.htm | title=Bell Book Collection | publisher=Microsoft Research | access-date=2006-09-20}}</ref> Among his other inventions were the [[parabolagraph]], the [[spirograph]], an electric bell used in trains, and a form of [[electric arc]] lamp.<ref name="Preece">{{cite journal | author=sir [[William Henry Preece]] | date=November 1882 | title=On a New Electric Arc Lamp | journal=[[Scientific American]] | volume=Supplement No. 360 | url=http://www2.cddc.vt.edu/gutenberg/etext05/8036010h.htm#20 | access-date=2006-09-20 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060911125636/http://www2.cddc.vt.edu/gutenberg/etext05/8036010h.htm#20 | archive-date=2006-09-11 }}</ref>

He also published several works on [[statistics]], mathematical instruments, and practical applications of integration, including ''Les intégraphes'' (1886).<ref name="Abakanowicz" /> In France, he served as a government expert on electrification projects and worked on systems in cities such as [[Lyon]].<ref name="Klaputh"/> His patents and innovations brought him wealth and recognition, and in 1889 he was awarded the [[Legion of Honour|Légion d'honneur]].

[[File:Le château de Costaeres à Trégastel - PSIMG 4117.jpg|thumb|right|The Château de Costaérès built by Abakanowicz in Trégastel]]
In the 1890s, Abakanowicz retired to a small island in [[Trégastel]], [[Brittany]], where between 1892 and 1896 he built the [[Château de Costaérès]], a [[Gothic Revival|neo-Gothic]] manor.<ref name="Monuments">{{cite web | title=Maison de villégiature dite Château de Costaérès | year=2005 | work=Monuments de France | url=http://www.monuments-de-france.org/notice_97154.html | access-date=2006-09-20 | language=fr | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070928002056/http://www.monuments-de-france.org/notice_97154.html | archive-date=2007-09-28 }}</ref> Although the construction was not completed during his lifetime, the castle became a meeting place for the Polish émigré community in France. Frequent guests included [[Aleksander Gierymski]], [[Władysław Mickiewicz]], [[Leon Wyczółkowski]], and [[Henryk Sienkiewicz]]. Sienkiewicz completed ''[[The Teutonic Knights (novel)|The Teutonic Knights]]'' and ''[[The Polaniecki Family]]'' at Abakanowicz's villa in Saint-Maur and wrote ''[[Quo Vadis (novel)|Quo Vadis]]'' at the Château de Costaérès.<ref name="Klaputh"/>

Abakanowicz died suddenly on 29 August 1900. In his will, he appointed Sienkiewicz as the guardian of his only daughter, [[Zofia Pstrokońska|Zofia]], who later graduated from the [[London School of Economics]] and the [[University of Paris|Sorbonne]], and was murdered during World War II at the [[Auschwitz concentration camp]].

== Legacy and identity ==
Abakanowicz’s nationality has been described in different ways. He was born in the territory of the former [[Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth]], which by 1852 was part of the [[Russian Empire]]. Some contemporary documents list him as Russian due to political boundaries, while ''[[Encyclopædia Britannica]]'' refers to him as Lithuanian. However, his education, language, and social circle were predominantly Polish, and he is generally regarded as a Polish scientist and inventor.<ref name="Klaputh"/>

The surname ''Abakanowicz'', of [[Lipka Tatar]] origin, derives from a noble family of the [[szlachta]] associated with the [[Abdank coat of arms]].<ref name="Boniecki">A. Boniecki, ''Herbarz polski'', t. 1, Warszawa 1899, s. 17.</ref><ref name="Uruski">S. Uruski, ''Rodzina. Herbarz szlachty polskiej'', t. 1, Warszawa 1904, s. 1.</ref><ref>[http://www.apropospage.com/uchebnik/abc/abc.html Выдающиеся математики - биографические сведения] {{Webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071028023539/http://www.apropospage.com/uchebnik/abc/abc.html |date=28 October 2007 }}</ref>
